card.name: Khorovod
card.tagline: Russia’s ancient circle dance — pagan-Slavic women joining hands in a turning ring, surviving Christianization and Soviet bans alike.
card.profile: The khorovod or horovod (Russian: хоровод, Ukrainian: хоровод, корогод, Polish: korowód) is the Slavic name for a folk dance combining circle dance and chorus singing, similar to the choreia of ancient Greece.
card.insight: Khorovod survived a thousand years of cultural pressure: the Orthodox Church suppressed it for centuries as 'pagan ritual,' Peter the Great's Westernizing reforms marginalized it in favor of European court dance, and Soviet anti-religion campaigns banned its ceremonial use. Yet in every Russian village, women continued to dance the khorovod, and today the Pyatnitsky Folk Choir and Beryozka Ensemble carry the tradition onto international stages from Moscow to Tokyo.
